title: When inheritance violates the parent contract
answer: Yes, that is a strong sign the inheritance relationship is being misused. A subtype should remain substitutable for its parent and honor the parent's behavioral contract; otherwise callers using the parent type can receive surprising or invalid behavior. This idea is commonly associated with the Liskov Substitution Principle. AeroTopo's Product contract says every product supplies a meaningful `resolutionMetres()` and export behavior, so subclasses must preserve those semantics rather than redefine them incompatibly.
